response.title: what are the main differences between the Mango Power E, the Nature's Generator Powerhouse, the Growatt Infinity 2000 and the VTOMAN FlashSpeed 1500
response.answer:
The Mango Power E, Nature's Generator Powerhouse, Growatt INFINITY 2000, and VTOMAN FlashSpeed 1500 are all portable power stations, but they're designed for somewhat different purposes.

The biggest differences are battery capacity, maximum power output, expandability, portability, and home backup capabilities.

In general, the Mango Power E and Nature's Generator Powerhouse are better suited to substantial home backup, while the Growatt INFINITY 2000 and VTOMAN FlashSpeed 1500 are more portable options for camping, RVs, and shorter power outages.

These are the base-unit specifications, without additional batteries or solar panels. The Growatt figures refer to the original INFINITY 2000, not the newer 2000 PRO.

Illustrative estimates, not measured performance. Real runtime depends on load, inverter losses, temperature, and battery condition. Refrigerator power draw varies as the compressor cycles.

One important distinction: battery capacity (Wh) determines roughly how long your devices run, while AC output (W) determines which devices you can operate simultaneously.

The Nature's Generator has by far the strongest inverter, but that doesn't automatically mean it will run a refrigerator for the longest time, particularly given its lead-acid chemistry.

3. What the capacity differences mean

Here are estimated runtimes for common electrical loads, using 85% usable AC energy for the three LFP stations. The Powerhouse is excluded from this chart because AGM lead-acid usable capacity varies significantly with discharge rate and depth of discharge.

Illustrative estimates, not measured performance. Real runtime depends on load, inverter losses, temperature, and battery condition. Refrigerator power draw varies as the compressor cycles.

One important distinction: battery capacity (Wh) determines roughly how long your devices run, while AC output (W) determines which devices you can operate simultaneously.

The Nature's Generator has by far the strongest inverter, but that doesn't automatically mean it will run a refrigerator for the longest time, particularly given its lead-acid chemistry.
